title: Bays, oriels and towers for the Prairie Avenue 1904 programme (package K08, the kit)
status: Declared, generated and built to. T-2308 put the first two on a house: the bow and the canted bay on 1808 Prairie Avenue (keith_house_1808_prairie, form.bays), each resolved from its variant here by generators/archetypes/k01_frontage_params.py and held to tools/check_bay_kit.py's rules at both tiers.
rule: A bay, oriel or tower is a closed projection keyed to its host wall: its plan starts and ends ON the wall's outer face, it never reaches behind it, and the wall closes it. Its plan is a polyline, a segmental bow, a circle or a regular polygon, cut by the wall plane; its walls rise from a plinth on grade or from corbel courses that step back into the wall, banded at each floor, and are capped by an eaves (soffit and fascia) and a roof whose planes are the plan's own lines lifted at one pitch, so hips fall where the planes meet and a curved plan takes a cone. Its windows are K06 openings, each a closed recess, placed by bearing or by fraction along the plan; on a curved run the whole opening, glass included, is bent to the curve. Every curve is cut finely enough that a near view sees no facet, and its normals follow the true curve so the shading does not band; the light tier cuts it coarser and drops the sash detail but keeps the silhouette. The sizes are data here and the generator reads them; tools/check_bay_kit.py rebuilds every variant and holds the built geometry to this file.

frame._doc: World frame of a built variant, the K01 frame: +X along the host wall to the right, +Y up, +Z out of the wall's outer face (z = 0). Grade is y = 0. A bearing is measured about the plan's centre from straight out of the wall (0) toward +X (positive).

parts._doc: The working sizes every variant starts from. A variant may override any of them under its own `overrides`.

wall.rule_source: RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md section Starting ranges: Solid exterior wall / reveal
wall.note: The bay's masonry wall. Its thickness sets how deep every window's reveal and recess can run.

plinth.note: A bay standing on grade stands on a stone plinth, proud of its wall: the foundation the reconstruction rules ask for ('bays have foundations or corbels').

floor_band.note: A stone string course at every floor line between storeys, mitred round every corner of the plan and bent round every curve.

eaves.note: The roof's edge: a soffit from the wall face out to a fascia 0.3 m beyond it, and a fascia 0.2 m deep whose top edge is the roof's eaves line.

corbel.note: An oriel stands on stone courses each stepped out over the one below. A course may oversail the one beneath by no more than 0.65 of its own height (the bracketing rule a corbel table is laid to), and the lowest still bears on the wall by at least 0.08 m.

recess.note: How deep a window's K06 recess runs behind the bay's outer face, glass, blind and curtain inside it. K06's own specimen runs 0.95 m back; inside a bay the recesses of neighbouring windows share the bay's plan, so they are cut shorter and the check holds every one inside the bay and clear of every other.

finial.note: A turned spike at a cap's apex, in the cap's own copper.

curves._doc: How finely a curved run is cut, and what that buys. A run is cut into slabs no wider than max_seg_deg of its arc; the chord of a slab then falls inside its arc by the sagitta R(1 - cos(step/2)). Normals are the true curve's, per vertex, so a slab's edge does not shade as a crease.

light.note: The light tier: a far view's copy. Curves cut at 15 degrees, so a 1.6 m tower's outline falls inside its true circle by at most 14 mm; windows keep their hole, reveal, sill, head band, glass and recess and lose their sash bars, blind and curtains. Its silhouette is held to the full tier's within max_sagitta_m.

roofs._doc: A roof's planes are the plan's own lines (or circle), offset out to the eaves and lifted at one pitch: the height over any point is eaves + pitch x its distance in from the nearest roof line. Over a polygon that is a hipped roof, trimmed at its hips where the planes meet; over a circle it is a cone. A bay's roof lines are its own runs only, so the roof leans against the wall and the wall closes it; a tower's are its whole ring, so its cap is a full pyramid or cone and a back face closes it where the wall plane cuts it. `covering` names the K04 fabric (data/components/prairie_1904/k04_roofs.json) a house will bind; the kit draws its flat colour.

costs._doc: Triangle budget per variant, as built, the board excluded. A variant over its budget is refused, so a kit change that bloats every bay in the town is caught here, before any house is built from it.

_variants_doc: plan: polyline (points [x, z] from the left junction to the right, both on z = 0), bow (a segmental arc on its chord), circle (radius, centre proud of the wall) or polygon (sides, circumradius, centre proud, a face square to the front). base: 'grade' stands on a plinth; a number is the height its corbel courses carry it at. storeys: heights from the base up, each with its windows: a K06 opening id, its clear size, its sill above the storey's floor, and where it sits (at: fractions of the plan's length, or at_deg: bearings about the plan's centre). roof: hip (or flat, pitch 0) or cone; covering is a K04 fabric.

variants.note: A two-storey rectangular bay, 2.6 m across and 1.2 m out, on a plinth: a wide segmental sash to the front and a narrow sash in each cheek, under a slate roof hipped against the wall.
The commonest Prairie Avenue bay: canted at 45 degrees, 1.5 m of front and 1.1 m out, two storeys, a window in every face, the hips of its slate roof falling on its angles.
A segmental bow, 3.2 m on its chord and 0.9 m out (a 1.87 m radius), two storeys of three bent sashes, under a shallow copper cone that leans on the wall.
A full-height projection: a shallow three-storey pavilion 4 m wide and 0.6 m out, two windows a floor, finished with a deep cornice and a flat tin deck where a house's main roof would take it over.

windows.why_not_ordinary: an oriel's cheek light: narrower than an ordinary sash so it fits the canted cheek

variants.note: A canted upper oriel at the first floor, 1.3 m of front and 0.65 m out, carried on four stone courses stepped back into the wall, under a steep copper hip.
A round tower 3.2 m across, its centre 0.7 m proud of the wall so it stands three quarters clear, three storeys of bent sashes and a steep copper cone with a finial.
An octagonal tower on the same 1.6 m circumradius, a face square to the street and a window in it and each face beside it, under an eight-sided copper spire whose hips fall on its angles.
